objective: Define the canonical identity, authentication, authorization, session and device-security policy for NEXUS QUANT against the P03-A threat model and frozen G2 architecture, without provisioning runtime identity infrastructure.
scope: Define deny-by-default least-privilege RBAC and permission semantics
Separate Owner/user, A0-A10, specialists, service/workload, CI and future external integration identities
Define privileged phishing-resistant MFA direction using WebAuthn/FIDO-class authenticators
Define recovery and MFA-reset security requirements
Define session issuance, rotation, expiry, revocation, concurrency and reauthentication rules
Define step-up authentication for sensitive/high-risk actions
Define device registration, trust and risk signals without making country/location an authorization dependency
Bind authorization to resource, action and environment
Define Human Gate approval binding and anti-replay requirements
Define service/workload identity direction and non-human credential rules
Create machine-readable role/permission/authentication policy and diagrams
Map implementation and validation ownership to downstream P03/P04/P23/P24 work
out_of_scope: Provision an identity provider or directory
Create production accounts, credentials or API keys
tests: Policy traces to P03-A threats and FROZEN_G2 trust/authority boundaries
Every privileged human role requires phishing-resistant MFA direction
Authorization is deny-by-default and resource/action/environment scoped
A5/A8 veto and Owner/Human Gate authority cannot be expanded by RBAC
Agent/tool permission is bounded by Task Contract and role intersection
Session fixation/replay/long-lived privileged session risks are addressed
MFA reset/recovery cannot silently bypass normal assurance
Country/location is not required or treated as trusted authorization evidence
No production IdP/account/credential/control is claimed implemented
security_tests: Session revocation and credential-change invalidation requirements are defined
Privileged step-up and sensitive-action reauthentication are defined
Human Gate replay/scope substitution protections are defined
Service/workload identities cannot use human ambient sessions
Recovery path preserves auditability and fail-closed semantics
rollback: Revert P03-B policy artifacts and shared state/catalog changes. No runtime identity service, credentials, accounts or trading authority are changed.
definition_of_done: Session and device policy is canonical
Human Gate and service-identity rules are canonical
Machine-readable policy and diagrams are canonical
Task Catalog and Current State are reconciled
